solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fare for Italians from Mediterranean island

definitions.meaning: first meaning: Italian cured sausages, in the plural
second meaning: a Greek island in the Saronic Gulf, site of a famous sea battle

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as Italian food coming from an island; 'from' only links two separate meanings of the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: Salamis are spicy Italian sausages, and Salamis is also an island near Athens, a homograph pairing.

clue.text: Person who shoots fish

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a photographer, one who snaps pictures
second meaning: a reddish food fish of warm seas

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoots' suggests a gun, but here it means taking photographs.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapper is informal for a photographer, and the same word names a family of sea fish.

clue.text: Miss dictionary definition for 'caught with rope'

parts.note: a miss is a girl or lass
OED is the Oxford English Dictionary

explanation.surface: Someone looks up the dictionary's definition of a roping term.
explanation.definitionFit: To lasso is to catch an animal with a looped rope, so lassoed is the past participle meaning caught that way.

clue.text: Bishop, for example, with quarters in ecclesiastical residence

parts.note: a bishop is a chess piece, and chess pieces are called men
S and E, south and east, two quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A bishop with lodgings inside a church house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bishop' points to the church, but it is the chess piece, one of the men on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A manse is a minister's house, especially in Scotland, so it is a clergy residence.

clue.text: Pick Spanish or French article, in part

indicators.note: in places the article within the word for part

parts.note: a section is a part of something
le is the French masculine article; el, the Spanish one, fits the same slot too

explanation.surface: Someone choosing a foreign article from part of a text.
explanation.walkthrough: Either article works: SE+LE+CTION or S+EL+ECTION spell the same thing, hence 'Spanish or French'.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection is a choice, which is what a pick is as a noun.

clue.text: Choose to get rid of ground-breaking device

parts.note: to choose is to pick
to axe is to get rid of, as with jobs

explanation.surface: An instruction to select a pioneering invention and then scrap it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground-breaking' sounds like innovative, but the tool literally breaks ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A pickaxe is a digging tool with a pointed head used to break up hard earth.

clue.text: Student at university I put in place

indicators.note: put in signals these letters being placed inside the abbreviation

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
up means in residence at university, as in going up to Oxford

explanation.surface: A student at college says they put themselves in their place.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at university is a British idiom for being in residence there.
explanation.definitionFit: A pupil is a learner at school, a synonym for student.

clue.text: Graves may be opened by this gang from part of Ireland

definitions.text: Graves may be opened by this

parts.note: Cork is an Irish county; Cork's means belonging to it, i.e. from there
a crew is a gang of people

explanation.surface: A sinister gang from County Cork is suspected of opening graves.
explanation.walkthrough: Graves is a Bordeaux wine, not a burial place; a gang from Cork would be Cork's crew.
explanation.definitionFit: A corkscrew draws the cork from a wine bottle, and Graves is a red or white wine from Bordeaux.

clue.text: A coach I have can be insulting

parts.note: a coach is a bus
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: Someone with a coach admits they can be rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' suggests a trainer but it is the vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: Abusive language is rude and offensive, so it is insulting.

clue.text: Area held by others, changing everything within it, we hear

indicators.note: held by means the abbreviation for area is put among the letters of others
changing everything means every letter of the pooled words is rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A region controlled by other people, who change all within it, so we're told.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Held by' just places A among the letters of OTHERS before the whole lot is rearranged. 'We hear' looks like a sound signal but belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the range within which a sound can be heard, so whatever is in it reaches our ears.

clue.text: Club in collection of weapons

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the London football club
second meaning: a store of arms

explanation.walkthrough: A club could be a weapon in a collection, but here it is the football team.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenal is a Premier League football club, and an arsenal is a stockpile of armaments.

clue.text: Someone chasing ship's officer around university

indicators.note: around means the officer's title surrounds the abbreviation

parts.note: a purser is the officer in charge of accounts on a ship

explanation.surface: A man running after a ship's officer around a campus.
explanation.definitionFit: A pursuer is one who follows or hunts another, the person doing the chasing.

clue.text: Frenchman demonstrated about short measure

parts.note: proven means shown to be true
CA, short for circa, means about
L is the abbreviation for litre

explanation.surface: A Frenchman was shown to have served a stingy measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short measure' sounds like cheating a drinker but is an abbreviated unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A Provençal is a native of Provence in southern France, so a Frenchman.

clue.text: Second expression of desire is smart

parts.note: a wish expresses a desire

explanation.surface: A second wish turns out to be clever.
explanation.definitionFit: Swish is informal for fashionable or elegant, the sense of smart in dress.

clue.text: With bright colour I had decorated anew

parts.note: red is a bright colour
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone redecorated using a vivid colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Redid means did again, and redoing a room means redecorating it.

clue.text: A great number upset about much agricultural business

indicators.note: about means the turned word goes round the next piece
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a myriad is a vast number
far means much, as in far better

explanation.surface: A crowd overturns something about a large farming firm.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upset' turns a word upside down, so it reads from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: A dairy farm keeps cattle for milk, a type of farming enterprise.

clue.text: Rebel got out of mountains urgently

indicators.note: got out of means the letters are extracted from inside the next words

explanation.surface: An insurgent hurriedly escaped from the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is one who rises in revolt against authority, so a rebel.

clue.text: Awful frauds rob supporter on crest of a wave

definitions.text: supporter on crest of a wave

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of the two words are a terrible mess, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Dreadful con artists steal a surfer's board.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfboard holds up a rider on the top of a breaking wave, so it supports them there.

clue.text: Opposition accepting rule by king, one from another country

indicators.note: accepting means taking the next piece inside

parts.note: a foe is an opponent
reign means rule
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: Opponents accept rule by a monarch who comes from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreigner is a person born in or coming from a different nation.

clue.text: Determined to capture attention, producing weapon

indicators.note: to capture means the word for determined holds the next piece inside

parts.note: firm means resolute, determined
to give an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Resolved to grab attention, someone brings out a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A firearm is a gun, a portable weapon that fires bullets.

clue.text: Course of treatment from doctor, e.g., I mentioned

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken from within the next stretch of words

explanation.surface: A patient reports a treatment plan from a doctor they mentioned.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed plan of diet, exercise or medication, a course of therapy.

clue.text: Charming woman accompanying Conservative inside

indicators.note: inside places the abbreviation within the other word

parts.note: with means accompanying

explanation.surface: A delightful woman goes along with a Tory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charming' means casting spells, not just being pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch works charms, that is spells, so she is literally a charming woman.

clue.text: Wound requiring, initially, blood transfusion — one can rest here

indicators.note: transfusion signals the letter being put into the other word

parts.note: wound, as in coiled, means twined

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An injury needing a blood transfusion leaves the patient resting in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wound' is the past tense of wind, not an injury.
explanation.definitionFit: A twin bed is one of a matching pair of single beds, a place to sleep.

clue.text: Someone no long popular is not totally penniless, we hear

indicators.note: we hear means the phrase is spoken, and a like-sounding word is the one written

parts.note: someone penniless hasn't a bean, so one who is not totally broke has a bean

explanation.surface: A faded celebrity is apparently not quite broke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not a bean' is British slang for no money at all.
explanation.definitionFit: A has-been is a person whose fame or success is past, no longer in favour.

clue.text: Girl embracing golf or another sport

indicators.note: embracing means the name wraps round the next letter

parts.note: Ruby is a girl's name
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A girl takes up golf, or perhaps some other game.
explanation.definitionFit: Rugby is a ball game played with an oval ball, one sport among many.

clue.text: Places where people can read overlapping signs

indicators.note: overlapping means the two signs share a letter where one ends and the next begins

parts.note: Libra and Aries are two signs of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Somewhere people can read signs that overlap.
explanation.walkthrough: LIBRA ends with the A that starts ARIES, so the shared letter appears once.
explanation.definitionFit: Libraries are buildings where books are kept to be borrowed or read.

clue.text: Source of ego, id, etc

parts.note: ego, id and etc are all words or abbreviations taken from the ancient language of Rome

explanation.walkthrough: Ego and id suggest Freud and psychology, but the source asked for is the language the words come from.
explanation.definitionFit: Ego means I, id means it and etc abbreviates et cetera, all borrowed from the classical Roman tongue.

clue.text: Like many flying from Russia via Norway

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the next few words

explanation.surface: Many travellers fly from Russia by way of Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many flying' suggests airline passengers, but it means birds.
explanation.definitionFit: Avian means relating to birds, and most birds fly.

clue.text: Aggressive colonist confused many, taken in by cunning

indicators.note: taken in by means the jumbled letters go inside the next word

parts.note: art means cunning or craft

indicators.note: confused means the letters of many are jumbled

explanation.surface: An aggressive settler confused the crowd through trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonist' suggests a settler, but an ant lives in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Army ants live in huge colonies and raid in swarms, preying on other insects.

clue.text: Friendly inquiry about my intelligence

definitions.meaning: second reading: the question ...?, asking whether one is clever enough

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word into three: am I able?
explanation.definitionFit: Amiable means genial and pleasant in manner, a synonym of friendly.

clue.text: A couple of servants carrying cross for islander

indicators.note: carrying means the pair holds the next letter between them

parts.note: a man is a manservant, so two servants give the word twice
X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: Two servants bear a cross for a man from an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manxman is a native of the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea.

clue.text: Island city in uproar about dreadful nude

indicators.note: about means the noise word goes round the jumbled letters

parts.note: a din is a loud noise or uproar

indicators.note: dreadful signals that the letters of nude are a mess, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A city on an island is in an uproar over a shocking naked person.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunedin is a city on New Zealand's South Island.
